# Energy and motion

These notes combine short definitions, worked examples, equations, and a comparison table.

## Kinetic energy

**Definition.** Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because it is moving.

For mass $m$ and speed $v$, the kinetic energy is

$$
E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2.
$$

If a 2 kg object travels at 3 m/s, its kinetic energy is 9 J. Doubling its speed multiplies this energy by four.

### Worked example

1. Identify the mass and speed.
2. Square the speed.
3. Multiply by half the mass.

> **Exam tip:** Include the unit and show substitutions before the final answer.

## Comparing quantities

| Quantity | Symbol | SI unit | Typical calculation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Speed | $v$ | m/s | distance / time |
| Acceleration | $a$ | m/s² | change in speed / time |
| Force | $F$ | N | mass × acceleration |

## Why the distinction matters

A force changes motion, whereas energy describes a system's capacity to do work. Keeping the two ideas separate makes it easier to choose the right equation.[^source]

[^source]: A short footnote used to check scholarly notes.
